q: For everyday use, the standard for measuring length may be a yard stick, ruler, _____ and so on.
e: Common everyday instruments for measuring length include yard sticks, rulers, and metre sticks.

q: Lengths are usually measured in metre, centimetre or _____.
e: Common units for measuring length are the metre, centimetre, and millimetre.
For greater lengths, the kilometre is the appropriate unit of measurement.

q: For measuring several metres (m), the suitable instrument is a _____.
e: A measuring tape is the most suitable instrument for measuring lengths of several metres.

q: The accuracy of a measuring tape is _____.
e: According to Table 1.3, the accuracy of a measuring tape is $1	ext{ mm}$ or $0.1	ext{ cm}$.

q: For measuring several centimetres (cm) to $1 ext{ m}$, the suitable instrument is a metre rule or _____.
e: A metre rule or half-metre rule is suitable for lengths between several centimetres and 1 metre.

q: For measuring between $1 ext{ cm}$ and $10 ext{ cm}$, the suitable instrument is _____.
e: Vernier calipers are the suitable instrument for measuring lengths between $1	ext{ cm}$ and $10	ext{ cm}$.

q: The accuracy of Vernier calipers is _____.
e: Vernier calipers provide an accuracy of $0.1	ext{ mm}$, which is equal to $0.01	ext{ cm}$.

q: For measuring less than $2 ext{ cm}$, the suitable instrument is a screw gauge or _____.
e: A screw gauge, also known as a micrometer, is used for measuring very small lengths (less than $2	ext{ cm}$).

q: The accuracy of a screw gauge (Micrometer) is _____.
e: The screw gauge (micrometer) has the highest accuracy among common length instruments, at $0.01	ext{ mm}$.
